channel.title: Abhi Singh
channel.description: Notes on AI enablement: how organisations help people actually use AI at work.

item.title: Your staff will soon build their own apps
item.description: Microsoft says Copilot Code will be generally available in December. Your staff will be able to build apps by describing them in plain words.

item.title: Have the conversation first, then make the document
item.description: Office in Copilot is now generally available, so a Copilot chat can turn straight into a Word document, a workbook or a deck.

item.title: Mask it before you paste it
item.description: This was a Sunday project. I'd been meaning to make time for it, because I think a lot of people could use it.

item.title: A free AI enablement starter kit
item.description: Most of what an organisation needs to start with AI is already free on GitHub. The hard part is choosing, setting it up and teaching it.

item.title: People are learning with AI anyway
item.description: 63% of US workers who use AI at work say it teaches them skills their employer never formally trained them on.

item.title: AI workflows in Teams, if the app is on
item.description: Microsoft Teams now has AI workflow templates in the Workflows app. Whether you see them depends on one admin setting.

item.title: Start a deck from your best deck
item.description: Copilot in PowerPoint can now take its look from a deck you attach. It's a better starting point than a blank prompt.

item.title: Click the link to what Copilot changed
item.description: When Copilot changes your Excel workbook, it now gives you a link straight to what it changed. I'd click it every time.

item.title: Two outages, one question
item.description: Microsoft 365 went down on 12 November, Copilot included. The next day, the US grounded departing flights for more than five hours.

item.title: The RBA's early read on AI and jobs
item.description: Around three-quarters of firms the RBA talks to say AI hasn't changed their headcount in the past year. The early signs are in who's being hired.

item.title: Australia's draft guide puts trust first
item.description: The federal government has released a draft guide on adopting AI at work. The minister says trust with the workforce is the key.

item.title: Gemini in Gmail reaches every Workspace user
item.description: Gemini in Gmail is coming to every Google Workspace user aged 18 and over. It's on by default.

item.title: Share a Gemini skill, and you share a copy
item.description: Google now lets teams share Gemini skills in Workspace. What you share is a copy, and your later edits don't reach it.

item.title: Jensen Huang and what his work built
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA's CEO this week. I like him, I admire what he built, and I'm still working out what to make of it.

item.title: UK amendment would let ministers set rules on AI agents
item.description: A proposed UK amendment would let ministers set rules on how organisations deploy and report on AI agents. It isn't law yet.

item.title: Gemini skills are personal. Sharing them is the organisation's job.
item.description: Gemini's new Customize hub lets each person build their own skills. Google's announcement describes admin controls for the connected apps, not the skills.

item.title: Edit a whole deck with Gemini in Slides
item.description: Gemini in Google Slides can now edit a whole deck from one prompt. There's no admin control for it.

item.title: Copilot gets Home, skills in Chat and an always-on agent
item.description: Microsoft's Copilot app now brings Chat and Cowork into one place. An always-on agent with its own mailbox is due on Frontier in November.

item.title: A policy exists, but does anyone know what's in it?
item.description: More than half of diginomica's digital leaders have an AI governance policy. Only 14% wrote it within the technology team alone.

item.title: Editing files inside Gemini chat
item.description: You can now create and edit files inside the Gemini chat, and there's no admin control specific to this feature.

item.title: Anthropic's reports on what AI spend produces
item.description: Anthropic now offers Claude Enterprise customers reports on what their AI spend produces. The vendor is helping to measure the value of its own product.

item.title: Walmart's 27% confidence gain
item.description: Walmart says associates who took OpenAI training reported a 27% confidence gain. It's an encouraging number, and it leaves the next question open.

item.title: Check the sources in Fill with Gemini
item.description: Fill with Gemini in Google Sheets now shows the web sources behind each cell. That makes a simple habit possible before anyone trusts a filled column.

item.title: Uber scales before showing pilot results
item.description: Uber is rolling ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 employees. The announcement doesn't say how the pilot went.

item.title: Improving my LinkedIn workflow on a Saturday afternoon
item.description: Today afternoon, I set out to improve the AI workflow behind my LinkedIn posts.
